name: stri_match_all
title: Extract Regex Pattern Matches, Together with Capture Groups

origin.description: Extract every regular-expression match and its capture groups.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: regex
arguments.text: A regular expression forwarded to stri_match_all_regex.

origin.details: This is an alias of stri_match_all_regex. The pattern is the regex argument. A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Column 0 is the whole match. A group that did not participate is cg_missing. A miss fills that pattern's own columns with cg_missing, and extra columns beyond that pattern stay NA. A missing string stays NA. Named groups label the columns when pattern is a single pattern. The first column name is empty. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive.
origin.example:
result <- stri_match_all("a1b2", regex = "([0-9])")[[1]]
cat(paste0('stri_match_all("a1b2", regex = "([0-9])") returns ', paste(result[1, ], collapse = ", "), ' and ', paste(result[2, ], collapse = ", "), '.\n'))

translation.description: Extract every regular-expression match and its capture groups.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Regular expression, missing value, or list of those. An empty pattern yields NA.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: If true, a string with no match contributes a matrix with no rows.

arguments.name: cg_missing
arguments.text: Text used for a group that did not participate. The default is NA.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: None, or a dict of only the regex settings that were supplied.

translation.details: This is the same function as stri_match_all_regex. A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Column 0 is the whole match. A group that did not participate is cg_missing. A miss fills that pattern's own columns with cg_missing, and extra columns beyond that pattern stay NA. A missing string stays NA. Named groups label the columns when pattern is a single pattern. The first column name is empty. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive. Each element is a matrix with that pattern's groups. A miss is one cg_missing row unless omit_no_match is true.
translation.value: A list of matrices, each a list of rows.
translation.example:
from stringi.regex import stri_match_all
result = stri_match_all("a1b2", "([0-9])")[0]
print('stri_match_all("a1b2", regex = "([0-9])") returns ' + ', '.join(result[0]) + ' and ' + ', '.join(result[1]) + '.')
